description: Source-backed AST syntax cases for the dima-rust parser/tokenizer/scanner port. Generated from the actual TypeScript syntax modules; do not hand-edit. Source parity is recorded separately from five fixture categories that implement two user-approved improvements: scanner/template scanning (item 4) and nested parse diagnostics (item 5). The four approved optimizations are performance-only.

operations.parse: engine.parse(input.source) -> Result<CompiledProgram, Diagnostic>; expected is {outcome:"program",ast} or {outcome:"diagnostic",diagnostic}.
operations.scan: engine.scan_template(input.source) -> Result<Vec<SourceSegment>, Diagnostic>; expected.segments carry UTF-16 spans.
operations.compiled-template: engine.compile_template(input.source); text/expr/unclosed plans match expected.segments; expression diagnostics are absolute to the original template source.
operations.unescape: surface="rendered" calls unescape_rendered_text(&str) with string input only. surface="literal" calls the now-public tokenizer literal unescape with string input.

limits.note: Corpus cases are far below the limits; benchmarks include the 128 nesting boundary as source-only definitions.

contract.spanConvention: UTF-16 code-unit, half-open [start,end). Scanner/plan spans and compiled-plan diagnostics are absolute to the input template. Parse diagnostics are relative to the parse input. For source-parity errors the exact TypeScript message is the source fact; code is the contract enum mapping and span is derived metadata that the adapter may relax to bounds. The legacy expectation of an approved case keeps that same derived code/span convention: it reproduces the source result, not a new TypeScript fact. Approved default diagnostics carry exact additive code/message/span.

diagnosticCodes.UNEXPECTED_CLOSING: A closer does not match the innermost open delimiter (message names the closer).
diagnosticCodes.UNCLOSED_DELIMITER: An opener token has no matching closer (message names the opener).
diagnosticCodes.UNCLOSED_ARRAY: A literal array %[ reaches the end of input.
diagnosticCodes.UNCLOSED_QUOTE: A double-quoted string reaches the end of input.
diagnosticCodes.UNCLOSED_EXPRESSION: A compiled-template expression segment has no closing parenthesis; the plan retains its source and diagnostic.
diagnosticCodes.UNEXPECTED_TOKEN: A nested expression leaves tokens unconsumed; message is Unexpected token "<tok>" in nested expression.
diagnosticCodes.MISSING_VARIABLE_NAME: Legacy safe diagnosis for an empty variable name (used only by source-throw hardening fixtures).
diagnosticCodes.SOURCE_LIMIT: Resource limit (not present in this corpus).
diagnosticCodes.TOKEN_LIMIT: Resource limit (not present in this corpus).
diagnosticCodes.NODE_LIMIT: Resource limit (not present in this corpus).
diagnosticCodes.NESTING_LIMIT: Resource limit (only the 128 benchmark boundary exercises it conceptually; source-only).
diagnosticCodes.INVALID_GRAMMAR: Grammar preparation error (not present in this corpus).

contract.normalization: The raw TypeScript result is always stored in `source` (ast/error/thrown) and is never rewritten. `expected` is normalized to the finalized API. For source-parity cases expected.legacy equals expected.default and represents `source` with the same AST or exact message. Rendered unescape is string-only because the Rust API is &str; JS ToString coercion is intentionally not ported.

sourceParityNotice: This corpus is NOT a claim of full semantic parity. Every `source` value is the unmodified TypeScript result. `expected.legacy` represents it for source-parity cases; `expected.default` equals it except for five fixture categories implementing user-approved items 4 (scanner/template scanning) and 5 (nested parse diagnostics), plus explicitly labelled source-throw hardening. Rationale is stored per case.

userApprovedItems.note: Only items 4 and 5 change AST syntax behaviour in this fixture. Other approved items and the four optimizations are outside this syntax corpus; this file does not infer semantics for them.

item4.label: scanner/template scanning
item4.summary: Contraction-aware apostrophe scanning, literal-array bracket depth in expression scanning, and escape-aligned array item boundaries (an escaped closer stays item text). AC-1 also keeps a double quote inside a ${...} interpolation from ending the enclosing quoted template.

item5.label: nested parse diagnostics
item5.summary: Nested tokenizer errors propagate, including into compiled template expression plans; unconsumed tokens in interpolations and array items reject the parse with UNEXPECTED_TOKEN.

approvedOptimizationsNote: The four approved optimizations are performance/implementation concerns, not semantics. This corpus supplies their representative benchmark inputs (short/mixed/loop/plain8000/dense100/dense500/nested-array/nested-compute) and asserts no speedup; it does not encode optimisation flags.
benchmarkPolicy: Benchmark entries are source/workload definitions. Their expected fields describe the unmodified TypeScript source (segments, AST summary) and intentionally store no AST. Boundary-depth entries (nesting 128) are workload definitions; do not treat their expected fields as a required Rust success assertion at an exact resource-limit boundary.

extraction.imports: All import and export-from declarations are stripped; the selected declarations run in an isolated vm context with no require().

approvedCorrections.summary: Scanner subcase: an intra-word ASCII apostrophe does not open a single-quoted region, so contractions inside an expression scan as valid. The same category also keeps a double quote inside a ${...} interpolation from ending the enclosing quoted template.
Nested-parse subcase: a tokenizer error inside an array item or template interpolation is propagated instead of being swallowed into a truncated node/text segment.
Nested-parse subcase: an interpolation with unconsumed tokens rejects the whole parse with an UNEXPECTED_TOKEN diagnostic instead of silently dropping the tail.
Nested-parse subcase: an array item with unconsumed tokens rejects the whole parse with an UNEXPECTED_TOKEN diagnostic instead of silently dropping the tail.
Scanner subcase: [ ] depth is tracked inside an expression so a ) inside an array item does not end the expression; quote and escape handling is unchanged.

combinedApprovals.note: Occurrences that exercise two approved improvements at once. The corpus still has exactly five fixture categories: `approved.code` is the primary category (AC-5 scanner array/bracket context) and `approved.combinedCategories` records the nested-diagnostic policy (AC-2) the same occurrence also exercises. Their default expectations are additive spec, never source parity.

nodeTypesUnreachableFromParser.reason: No registry/parser handler constructs a custom node; custom nodes are an evaluator/consumer extension point.

approvedErrorContract.AC-1: Scanner category implementing item 4: intra-word apostrophes do not open a quote. The same category treats a double quote inside a ${...} interpolation as inner interpolation text rather than a terminator for the enclosing quoted template; the category code/name is retained for schema compatibility.
approvedErrorContract.AC-2: Nested-parse category implementing item 5: nested tokenizer errors (array items and template interpolations) propagate in default mode. Legacy keeps the source result, including its exact [Parse error: ...] text segments, and that includes an inner error the source template parser caught rather than a top-level throw. Where the source throws, legacy must only return a safe diagnostic; the recorded MISSING_VARIABLE_NAME outcome is the current expected legacy diagnosis, not a source fact.
approvedErrorContract.AC-3: Nested-parse category implementing item 5: an interpolation with unconsumed tokens rejects the whole parse with UNEXPECTED_TOKEN and message Unexpected token "<tok>" in nested expression. It is NOT an error-text template AST in default mode; legacy retains the exact TypeScript truncation.
approvedErrorContract.AC-4: Nested-parse category implementing item 5: an array item with unconsumed tokens rejects the whole parse with UNEXPECTED_TOKEN and the first unconsumed token span; no truncated AST is produced. This includes a bracket-group item (unprefixed [b,c] / [a]), whose rejected tail is proved to be real syntax by the same item text with the required %[ prefix.
approvedErrorContract.AC-5: Scanner category implementing item 4: [ ] depth inside an expression is tracked for ) termination while quote/escape behaviour is preserved, and an escaped closer stays inside the item text. In compiled templates the same occurrence is combined with AC-2 (see combinedApprovals): the bracket-aware scanner keeps one expression segment and the nested tokenizer then rejects a stray closer or missing array-item closer inside it, so the expression program is a diagnostic instead of the legacy unclosed segment or silently truncated AST.

caveats: Approved diagnostics (AC-2/AC-3/AC-4) carry additive code/message/span; only the source-parity exact message and source AST/text segments are facts from the TypeScript oracle.

AC-1's contraction rule is limited to an ASCII word character on both sides of the apostrophe; possessives after punctuation or a nested expression are outside that rule and are not asserted. Within AC-1, a double quote inside a ${...} interpolation does not close the enclosing quoted template; that quote-state correction is scanner policy (item 4), separate from the item-5 nested-parse diagnostics.

The scanner does not treat quotes in top-level plain text as shields for start tokens (e.g. "${%(x)}" splits into text/expr/text). This is legacy behaviour and is preserved; no approved fix changes it.
Malformed bracket depth inside an expression (an unclosed "[" before the final ")") has unspecified default scan behaviour and is deliberately not asserted.

Legacy quirks are preserved on purpose and only in legacy mode: %[a,b][] is not accepted as a length accessor, an unprefixed [b,c] inside an array item is not a nested array (legacy keeps the literal "[" and drops the tail, while the default mode rejects the leftover tokens per AC-4), and %[%()] parses a getVar named ")".

AC-5 compiled occurrences are not source parity: the bracket-aware scanner keeps one expression segment where the source scanner ended the call at the first ), and the approved nested tokenizer then reports a stray closer or a missing array-item closer as that expression program. The legacy plan keeps the exact source split/unclosed segment.

An escaped closer (%[a\]b, c]) stays item text for the scanner, so the default parse reads the array item boundary the same way; the source parser reports the array's own final ] as an unexpected closer. The default AST is derived from the item tokenizer and literal unescape, not copied from an engine result.

Lone UTF-16 surrogates are excluded because they are not valid Rust String values; valid astral characters and JavaScript whitespace code units are covered. U+0085 NEL is not ECMAScript whitespace and must stay literal (js_compat).

Parse rules that are not part of the approved fixes are retained even when surprising: extra tokens after *(...) and %(x ...) keep their source behaviour, empty ternary consequents remain supported, and loop syntax errors remain literal [Loop error: ...] nodes.
unescape_rendered_text is string-only in the finalized API; non-string/ToString coercion is intentionally outside this port. The literal unescape helper is public and string-only.
The four approved optimizations are performance-only. No timing or speedup is recorded, and benchmarks never evaluate an expression or touch IO.

Deep benchmarks (nested arrays 8..128, compute 32..128) are source-only definitions: the corpus stores no deep AST, keeping the fixture well under serde_json default recursion limits. Source-parity cases stay at AST depth <= 16.

Spans are UTF-16 half-open offsets. Legacy TypeScript exposed no spans: source-parity spans, and the legacy code/span of an approved case, are derived from the real token/segment stream for verification, not from source facts. Approved default code/message/span are additive spec and are asserted exactly.

approved.summary: Scanner subcase: [ ] depth is tracked inside an expression so a ) inside an array item does not end the expression; quote and escape handling is unchanged.
approved.rationale: The literal array has one item containing an escaped closer and one plain item. The real item tokenizer reads `a\]b` as a single literal token (literal unescape: a]b) and `c` as a literal, so the escape changes the text, not the item boundary. The source parser instead reports the array's own closing ] as an unexpected closer because its delimiter validation ignores the escaped bracket. Quote/escape handling is unchanged; only array bracket context is corrected, and the raw source result is kept verbatim in `source`.

approved.summary: Scanner subcase: [ ] depth is tracked inside an expression so a ) inside an array item does not end the expression; quote and escape handling is unchanged.
approved.rationale: Bracket depth keeps the whole call as one expression segment (AC-5). The nested tokenizer then rejects the stray ) inside the array item instead of ignoring it (AC-2), so the expression program is an UNEXPECTED_CLOSING diagnostic at that closer. The same nested case follows a text segment, so the absolute plan diagnostic starts at the expression offset.

approved.summary: Scanner subcase: an intra-word ASCII apostrophe does not open a single-quoted region, so contractions inside an expression scan as valid. The same category also keeps a double quote inside a ${...} interpolation from ending the enclosing quoted template.
approved.rationale: A double quote inside a ${...} interpolation is inner interpolation text, not a terminator for the enclosing quoted template. The source scanner loses the outer quote state at that inner quote and finishes the call at the ) inside it, so the rest of the call becomes literal text. The corrected quote state keeps the whole call as one expression followed by the literal tail; the expression itself is a valid source parse (asserted above), and the compiled plan uses that unchanged AST. This is the approved item-4 scanner category, distinct from the item-5 nested-parse diagnostics.
